title: Python: the gate reads a LATER unconditional def or class as overriding an earlier binding too (general later-binding-overrides rule, split from GCLI-126)
description: Split from GCLI-126 by the leader's ruling. moduleBindingGate unions every def, class and import binding of a name as alternatives. GCLI-126 makes an always-running LAST IMPORT override the earlier bindings (when every binding has a line, no other binding shares the last one, and the last is an import that maySkipStatement does not skip); otherwise it reads every binding as before. Not done: the same override when the LAST unconditional binding is a def or a class ('from x import f' then an unconditional 'def f' reads {x.f, m.f}, Python binds m.f), a last binding that is an unconditional def or class after earlier conditional imports, and the general later-binding rule across kinds and arms. Over-flagging only: every edge in the union is a real alternative or a flagged superset, so soundness holds. Design change beyond GCLI-126's AC, for opum-doc to rank.

acceptanceCriteria.text: an unconditional def or class after earlier bindings overrides them in the gate, in both forms, red before and green after with callees pinned and the full bin delta
a conditional last binding, a binding without a line and a same-line tie keep every alternative
a mutant that treats the last binding as conditional is observed red
the five-pin corpus diff against dev is script-asserted with every moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed, including a multiplyBound-to-single move, comes to opum-doc before the clear
